title: Accelerate a complete 64-axis Clifford projection by 40.6% (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped implementation-equivalence proof with finite conformance and empirical performance evidence. A new adjacency-bitset quadratic Gauss-sum evaluator reduces a complete fixed 64-axis, four-source Clifford projection calculation by **40.6%**. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

```diff
 complete finite-span calculation
- polynomial-substitution Gauss elimination
+ diagonal-coefficient and adjacency-bitset elimination
  same Choi construction, complete kernel, exact solve and output
```

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Ali Romman retains PR5727's contraction engine, exact finite-span solver, scientific results, source set and complete replay. PR5704, PR5526, PR5698 and their retained native/controller/compiler lineage keep their credit. Quadratic Gauss-sum elimination is classical. Only research/bitset-gauss-elimination is added.

## Evidence

Five alternating fresh-process pairs, including startup, all source checks, five circuit constructions, Choi states, all 25 kernel entries, exact normal-equation solve and output:

- Baseline median 0.445115 s, range 0.435274–0.505192 s.
- Bitset median 0.264530 s, range 0.264092–0.320435 s.
- All ten complete outputs have SHA256 9e9ca672563db4c1d3a281be16c2fdcd798ae96de4fd9cd8c2e9ca1ce624effa; zero errors. Raw samples and source hashes are in BENCHMARK.json. Host is shared macOS arm64 with CPython 3.12.15 and 18 logical cores. These are local fixture measurements, not a cross-platform claim.

Separate profiles put about half the baseline projection time in Gauss elimination; Choi construction and remaining affine work limit the gain. The original complete inventory replay has only about 3.5% in Gauss elimination, and its overall timing gain is inconclusive. The advance claim's wider performance prediction was withdrawn in the linked scope update.

Local warning-strict normal/optimized direct and registered replays pass 67,732 exhaustive small sums, 64 larger literal sums, 40 dense binomial fixtures through dimension 256, ten invalid-input and four semantic controls. Every one of 82,237 Gauss calls in the inherited complete consumer is compared with the original implementation; its entire committed RESULT.json is still required. The consumer replay is a conformance test, not an audit deliverable. Source corruption and two algorithm mutations reject. Registered commands took 11.16 and 11.25 seconds, below their 120-second limits.

Committed-byte/mode and source-history checks pass for 33 package/input files. Official export integrity checks all 20 declared inputs. Normal and optimized direct checks pass in a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH; all 34 exported files retain their SHA256 and modes.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/bitset-gauss-elimination/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B -O research/bitset-gauss-elimination/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bitset-gauss-elimination
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/bitset-gauss-elimination --check-source-history
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/bitset-gauss-elimination/benchmark.py --workload projection --output /absolute/new/scratch/benchmark.json
```

Any CPython 3.12 interpreter may replace the local path. The direct verifier prints PASS_BITSET_GAUSS_ELIMINATION and a generated file-hash-bound receipt.

## Limitations

The implementation accepts at most 256 Boolean phase variables. The equivalence argument is written, with finite corroboration. Performance is claimed only for this deterministic complete calculation. No new approximation optimum, production-search timing, selected replay installation, native/physical bill, dirty restoration, precision/tape/compiler/outer admission or multiplication theorem follows. Lean, Docker, the selected scientific cold replay, other hosts, independent human review and formal proof-kernel review are unrun or unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Reduce the remaining Choi/affine-substitution work with identical state output. Begin with one substitution from the optimized profile; no replacement is supplied here.
- Bind a real wider native-interface search and measure five alternating complete commands on another host. A named production consumer and cross-platform evidence remain absent.

## Related open work

- #2329 accelerates literal Clifford zero-state execution with gate tables in the historical cold617 consumer. This changes quadratic Gauss elimination in PR5727's compact contractions; it does not install or recheck that adapter.
- #6203 accelerates a nine-screen affine/vector replay by incremental polynomial-code rows. It changes a different consumer and computation; no Gauss-sum or fixed-projection timing is reported there.
- #6206 accelerates the H4 root replay through exact projective-normal reuse. Its root scans and timing fixture are separate from this phase-elimination workload.

The completion refresh examined all fifteen other account open PRs created since the advance claim. None studies this Gauss kernel or reports a competing value for the fixed 64-axis projection. No extra computations were run to check their results. Bounded live searches do not cover unpublished work or every historical diff.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/bitset-gauss-elimination)`, passed at head `4e50e98e4ee2c87139aa127de72aed9a74bfde4b` in [run 40913882642](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40913882642). The completed checks were read once and the run's exact head and successful conclusion confirmed. Hosted conformance does not certify the local performance percentage or independent scientific acceptance.

## Merge danger

**Door:** Two-way. **Blast radius:** One new opt-in research package and its declared replay. Predecessor bytes and the selected frontier are unchanged.
